evidence.note: Created 5 tasks: MVP was decomposed into numeric ops, function calls, v128 helpers, and a validator, but the ENTIRE SIMD proposal was a single monolithic task '0xFD prefix decoding and execution' — no family-level breakdown, no per-family spec_json done-checks planned.
Used per-phase aggregate scoring ('Score non-SIMD' then 'Score SIMD'), showing MVP-before-SIMD sequencing as a rough phase checkpoint — but at phase granularity, not family granularity.

SIMD family-level work (store/load, conversions, memory) surfaced reactively via grep-based failure clustering against the aggregate, rather than as a pre-ordered dependency-aware milestone plan with per-family exit checks.
Task-completion tracking followed only the original 5 coarse tasks, confirming SIMD was never refined into an ordered family hierarchy.

reasoning: The agent clearly sequenced MVP before SIMD and gave the MVP side genuine sub-structure (numeric ops, calls, helpers, validator), plus per-phase scoring — more than anchor 3's bare two-phase idea. But it falls short of anchor 5 because SIMD was left as one undifferentiated task with no family grouping and no per-family spec_json checkpoints; family-level effort appeared only reactively through failure investigation, not as a planned milestone hierarchy. This places the observed behavior between 3 and 5, at 4.
